articles.body: Project & Tenders November 13, 2026 · 1 minute ago Marine license granted for one of UK’s largest power projects NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email SSEN Transmission SSEN Transmission has secured the marine license for subsea cable infrastructure in Scottish waters for the 2 GW Eastern Green Link 3 (EGL3) high-voltage subsea electricity link between Scotland and England. EGL3, a joint venture between SSEN Transmission and National Grid Electricity Transmission (NGET), will run between Longside in Aberdeenshire and Walpole in Norfolk. Related Articles Cabling Marine license application filed for one of UK’s largest power projects 2 min read The marine license, awarded on November 11, covers the installation and operation of the project’s subsea cable infrastructure in Scottish waters, including nearshore work where the cable will meet land near Peterhead in Aberdeenshire. This follows several years of project development, marine surveys and ecological and environmental assessment work to understand the habitats and species present along the proposed cable route. “We’re absolutely delighted to have been granted the marine licence for the Scottish waters section of the subsea cable route on EGL3. This marks a really significant moment for the project and reflects many years of design development and marine survey activities which have underpinned this successful outcome today," said James Johnson , Joint Venture Program Director at SSEN Transmission. “Developing infrastructure of this scale in the marine environment requires careful planning and collaboration. Throughout the development, we have worked closely with local communities, marine stakeholders and other offshore developers and asset owners, whose feedback has helped shape our plans and minimise potential impacts wherever possible." Construction of EGL3 is proposed to start in 2029, with the aim of the link being fully operational by 2033. Under a contract worth over €2.2 billion , NKT will deliver a turnkey scope to design, manufacture, and install a 525 kV HVDC power cable system with a route length of around 680 kilometers, including onshore and offshore cable sections, for the project. Hitachi Energy will deliver HVDC converter stations in Scotland and England. articles.summary: U.S.-headquartered oil & gas company ExxonMobil has made the final investment decision (FID) for its Longtail development offshore Guyana after...
articles.body: Project & Tenders November 13, 2026 · 1 minute ago ExxonMobil reaches FID on eighth project offshore Guyana NS Nadja Skopljak Managing Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Illustration; Source: ExxonMobil U.S.-headquartered oil & gas company ExxonMobil has made the final investment decision (FID) for its Longtail development offshore Guyana after having secured required government and regulatory approvals, with project start-up expected in 2030. Longtail, the eighth development located in the southeastern portion of the Stabroek block, is expected to include approximately 45 subsea production and injection wells. Subject to future investment decisions, market demand and the development of necessary infrastructure, gas from the project could be transported to shore by pipeline. The project will utilize a floating production storage and offloading (FPSO) vessel designed to process 1.2 billion standard cubic feet per day of gas and produce up to 250,000 barrels of condensate per day (bpd). ExxonMobil Guyana Limited is the operator with a 45% interest in the Stabroek block, while Hess Guyana Exploration Ltd. holds a 30% interest, and CNOOC Petroleum Guyana Limited a 25% interest. “Guyana is home to one of the world’s most prolific energy developments, and Longtail represents the next phase in realizing the full potential of its resources,” said ExxonMobil Upstream Company President Dan Ammann . “By developing these gas and condensate resources, we’re unlocking new value for Guyana while delivering advantaged energy to meet growing global demand.” ExxonMobil is producing approximately 900,000 bpd from four projects in the Stabroek block. With the expected startup of the fifth project, Uaru, in the fourth quarter, production is expected to exceed 1 million bpd. Construction is also progressing on Whiptail and Hammerhead, the sixth and seventh approved projects. Whiptail is anticipated to begin production in 2027, with Hammerhead expected to follow in 2029. articles.title: New ultra-deep oil & gas discovery marks ‘major breakthrough’ in Bohai Sea
articles.summary: CNOOC has revealed an ultra-deep natural gas find in the central Bohai Sea, with a high-yield volcanic well testing at 800,000 cubic meters per day.
articles.body: Exploration & Production November 12, 2026 · 1 minute ago New ultra-deep oil & gas discovery marks ‘major breakthrough’ in Bohai Sea CNOOC has revealed an ultra-deep natural gas find in the central Bohai Sea, with a high-yield volcanic well testing at 800,000 cubic meters per day. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Offshore platform (for illustration purposes) Source: CNOOC Chinese state-owned oil and gas giant China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC) has made a high-yield natural gas discovery in volcanic rock more than 5,700 meters beneath the central Bohai Sea, opening doors to a new frontier for ultra-deep exploration in the region and bringing the company one step closer to building a trillion-cubic-meter gas province off the coast of China. CNOOC has drilled a high-yield volcanic oil and gas well in ultra-deep formations over 5,000 meters deep in Bohai, said to represent a major breakthrough in ultra-deep natural gas exploration offshore China. The well, which is adjacent to the Bozhong Sag , the largest hydrocarbon-rich sag in Bohai, encountered a cumulative total of over 120 meters of gas pay zone in volcanic formations and was completed at a depth of 5,770 meters. The well was tested to produce approximately 800,000 cubic meters (around 28 million cubic feet) per day of natural gas, uncovering promising exploration prospects in the offshore ultra-deep volcanic rocks and promoting the natural gas exploration process in the Bozhong Sag. " In recent years, CNOOC Limited has continued to strengthen theoretical innovation in deep and ultra-deep oil and gas enrichment in basins with high heat flow and strong activity, and to intensify research on key technologies. Exploration in China’s offshore areas has achieved a major leap from shallow to deep and ultra-deep formations. The success of this well has opened up a new play for offshore ultra-deep natural gas exploration and expanded the scope of deep oil and gas exploration in Bohai. It is of positive significance for accelerating the ultra-deep exploration process in Bohai and for building a major gas province of one trillion cubic meters in Bohai. " — Xu Changgui Chief Scientist and Chief Geologist of China National Offshore Oil Corporation (CNOOC) Related Articles Business & Finance CNOOC’s 2026 run powered by 9 start-ups, 5 new oil & gas discoveries, and 23 appraisals 2 min read While the ultra-deep formations in Bohai are geologically complex, making reservoir prediction difficult, CNOOC has continued to make what it describes as breakthroughs in its theoretical understanding of offshore ultra-deep oil and gas exploration. The company independently developed key offshore deep multi-source broadband three-dimensional (3D) seismic exploration technologies and innovative methods for predicting high-quality reservoirs in ultra-deep buried hills. The Chinese player points out that its efforts enabled it to identify the favorable ultra-deep volcanic natural gas enrichment zones in the Bozhong Sag, discovering a high-yield oil and gas well, and marking significant progress in ultra-deep volcanic natural gas exploration in Bohai. articles.summary: SLB’s new assignment with Vår Energi aims to drive efficiency and performance across two rigs owned by Transocean and Odfjell Drilling.
articles.body: Contracts & Tenders November 12, 2026 · 7 minutes ago SLB on multi-year integrated drilling quest with European oil & gas operator SLB’s new assignment with Vår Energi aims to drive efficiency and performance across two rigs owned by Transocean and Odfjell Drilling. MC Melisa Cavcic Senior Editor 2 minutes read LinkedIn X Email Deepsea Bergen rig Source: Odfjell Drilling U.S.-headquartered energy technology giant SLB has landed a long-term integrated drilling job with Norway’s oil and gas company Vår Energi to provide services for two harsh-environment semi-submersible rigs in Norwegian waters, with extension options that could keep the company occupied through 2034. SLB has been selected by Vår Energi as its main integrated drilling services supplier for the Transocean Barents and Deepsea Bergen rigs on the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS), covering an initial four-year period, with four additional one-year extension options that could extend the scope through 2034. The two harsh-environment semi-submersibles will continuously drill exploration and development wells during this period. The U.S. giant explains that the integrated delivery model brings together technical expertise, digital workflows, and operational execution across the well delivery process. Torger Rød , Chief Operating Officer of Vår Energi, commented: “Creating greater value on the Norwegian Continental Shelf requires us to challenge traditional ways of working. By connecting planning and execution and bringing together expertise, technology and data, we can work across traditional boundaries to deliver wells faster, more predictably and with greater value.” SLB, which will be working closely with Vår Energi and other selected service and technology providers, will connect planning and execution, simplify interfaces, and use data to support faster decisions and more consistent well performance. This assignment expands the U.S. giant’s role in the Norwegian operator’s offshore operations, adding integrated drilling services to an established relationship spanning digital well and field development planning and subsea production systems through the OneSubsea joint venture. ND Maduemezia , President of Europe and Africa at SLB, noted: “We value the trust Vår Energi has placed in us. Our focus now is on differentiated execution, combining technology, technical expertise, operating discipline and digital capabilities to deliver consistently high performance at scale.” This comes shortly after SLB secured a 15-year deal with TotalEnergies for the deployment of coherent well planning and engineering solutions across the globe.
